text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- U.S. decision to grant Jordan special consideration as a major non-NATO ally means Jordan will get free weapons from the U.S. but does not mean it has made a defence pact with Washington or that Jordanian military bases will be at Washington's disposal, Deputy Prime Minister Ensour says.
- King Hussein donates 120,000 dinars ($170,000) towards a Turkish carpet for al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem.
- Justice Minister Dughmi says compromise discussed over land rights in al-Hussein Palestinian refugee camp.
- Customs department says sales tax can be imposed on smuggled goods uncovered by customs.
- Deputy Central Bank governor says bank could intervene indirectly over appointment of senior administration in local banks.
- Jordan hails economic results of Middle East and North African conference in Cairo. Jordanian participants say Jordan emerged with a strengthened economic profile, but no dramatic business deals.
